title: Fibre care: bamboo yarn
subtitle: How to wash, block, and store crochet made from bamboo fibre
excerpt: Bamboo yarn is a plant-based fibre that feels silky and cool, drapes beautifully, and is naturally moisture-wicking. It also distorts more than wool under weight when wet and can stretch permanently if pulled while damp. Knowing how to wash and block bamboo crochet prevents distortion and keeps the fabric looking as good as when it was first made.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book (Storey Publishing). Pauline Turner, How to Crochet (HarperCollins).

glossaryTerms.definition: A yarn made from the cellulose fibres of bamboo plants, processed into a soft, silky fibre. It drapes well and has moisture-wicking properties but is heavier and more prone to stretching under wet weight than wool or cotton.
For bamboo yarn: soaking the finished piece, removing excess water by rolling in a towel, then laying flat and pinning to the correct dimensions. Never hang bamboo to dry while wet.

content.text: is a regenerated cellulose fibre, made from bamboo plant material that is processed into a silky, smooth filament. It is cool to the touch, naturally moisture-wicking, and drapes well. The challenge is that it is heavier than wool and stretches significantly under its own weight when wet. A bamboo garment hung on a peg to dry can stretch several centimetres longer than its finished dimensions.

items.name: Gentle wool wash or no-rinse wool wash
items.note: Bamboo is delicate and benefits from a gentle detergent rather than regular washing powder.

items.name: Clean, dry towels
items.note: For rolling to remove excess water

content.text: Check the yarn label. Most bamboo yarns are hand-wash only; some bamboo blends with cotton or wool may be machine-washable on a delicate cycle. Follow the label instruction.

For hand washing, fill a basin with cool or lukewarm water. Add a small amount of gentle detergent and dissolve it before adding the item. Hot water can cause bamboo to felt if it is blended with wool.
Submerge the item and gently press it underwater. Do not agitate, rub, or wring. Leave to soak for 5 to 10 minutes.
Lift the item out of the water supporting its full weight with both hands. Bamboo is very heavy when wet and will stretch if lifted by one corner.
Roll in a towel to remove excess water. Replace the towel and roll again if needed. The item should be damp, not dripping.

is the standard method. Lay the damp item flat on the blocking mat and pin to the correct dimensions. Never hang bamboo to dry: the wet weight will pull the fabric out of shape. Leave flat until completely dry, which can take 24 to 48 hours for dense pieces in humid conditions.

items.symptom: The garment is longer than planned after the first wash
items.cause: The wet weight of the bamboo fibre stretched the piece before it was laid flat to dry.
items.fix: Re-wet the piece and block it flat, pinning firmly to the original dimensions. Bamboo will often return to the blocked dimensions if re-wet and re-pinned.

items.symptom: The bamboo fabric feels stiff after washing
items.cause: Mineral deposits from hard water or too much detergent left in the fibre.
items.fix: Rinse thoroughly in fresh water, adding a small splash of white vinegar to the final rinse water to soften the fibre.

items.symptom: The yarn pills after a few wears
items.cause: Bamboo is a smooth fibre and pills less than wool, but friction against other surfaces can cause surface roughness.
items.fix: Turn the garment inside out for wearing and washing. If pills form, remove them with a fabric shaver on the lowest setting.

content.text: Store bamboo crochet folded flat rather than on a hanger. The weight of a folded garment is supported evenly; a hanger concentrates the weight at the shoulder points and slowly distorts the shape over time. Wrap in acid-free tissue paper if storing long-term.
